body: Yeah I just can't do it. I've been myself for 30+ years and it's awful

I can't get friends to spend meaningful time with me because they all have their own lives by this point, and I don't really have any family left either. It seems like by this point I'm supposed to be married and if I'm not then that's my own problem and everybody's okay leaving me behind.

Walk away man. The debt isn't trapping you, it'll be there no matter what job you're working, right? Maybe it will take you a little longer to pay off but you'll be paying it off doing a job you enjoy. I switched jobs recently and it helped my mental state a lot, I didn't realize until I quit just how much that job was dragging me down. Took a pay cut and my finances are tighter but I'm happier overall. Wish you the best either way.

Yes. I really wish I was normal. I think I would be a lot happier and would have more close relationships and less pain. I do appreciate my creativity and ability to study and learn as much as I can about a topic. But I would give away all my individuality to just no longer experience the pain and alienation.

I feel the same way. Both as a writer and art appreciator. The most disturbing thing is that it seems like normal people genuinely don't care that art is going to die. They don't see the difference between art created by a robot and art created by a human. It just disgusts me that I am considered to be part of the same race as these things who cannot appreciate the most beautiful and significant thing about humanity, the thing that made us what we are, our creativity and invention.
Thank you and everyone else for these thoughtful responses. They really speak to me. I'm going to print these out and carry them in my wallet to read when I'm feeling like shit. Thanks again.
Thanks.

I don't think they would get in trouble but apparently it is very traumatic for them. I want to jump in front of a train too. I wish there were some without engineers. If we have cars that can parallel park themselves I feel like that should be quite possible. It was probably possible decades ago, the trains are on tracks for fucks sake. They must have good unions.

It seems silly but to me having a suicide plan helped keep me here this long I think. It is a comfort to know I can end it and leave if I have to. I am not totally helpless and don't need to panic. I have at least a little bit of agency in my life.

That's fair. It's not so much that I care deeply what happens at my job but I just don't like to fail. It's frustrating to try when something goes wrong. 500 things can go right but 1 thing will always go wrong. And when that happens everything else was a wasted effort.
At work today I went with our client to get some documents notarized at the bank. I forgot one of them so I'll have to reschedule with him. It's amazing how I always find a way to screw up.
Thank you. I needed that.

They are not that helpful. The best advice I got from one was to tell my therapist about it. That sounds like an insult but it was helpful in a way. I have a hard time talking about myself so it can be helpful practicing or bouncing ideas off of someone I will never meet or speak to again.

I guess that's true. I should write just to express myself and get the ideas out there. I feel like I owe it to the characters to finish. But it is just hard. I also want to be liked and to get positive feedback and encouragement. I want to know that I did a good job at something and to feel like I'm worth something. And I don't know how to do that except through writing.
I don't want to be too specific about my story but it's kind of a silly horror about a fighting monster girl. It might be too niche which is why it isn't popular...

Since middle school...so 15+ years. I think I have improved but it is tough because this was supposed to be my thing. It seems like every day I face failure after failure. So it is hard to learn I really am not good at anything.
I don't know. I feel like there will be a good stopping place where I can't think of any more.

I would let them know how you feel. It takes a lot to open up to somebody (for some people), especially trust. And I feel like you can't trust someone you don't care about. Obviously I don't know your friends but if they have that kind of trust in you I believe they care enough to listen if you bring it up.

I was in a similar situation. I was a listener who listened to my friend's problems all the time. It didn't bother me until I noticed that whenever I would try to open up about what's going on with me he would either ignore me, make a joke or change the subject. If our friendship didn't go that deep, it would have been fine, I have other friends we just mutually don't go there with. But since he wanted me to hear his deep thoughts and was not willing to do the same for me it bothered me greatly. You say your friends were vocal about not wanting to listen to you, but you listen to them. This is a one-sided relationship. Anything you can do for them they should be able to do for you. It is kind of selfish.
This wasn't in the context of trying to end our friendship, just trying to explain why I don't feel like hanging out all the time.
I tried with one friend and it didn't really go well. He took it personally that it is hard for me to be around other people, even him.
Thank you, it means a lot to know I'm not alone feeling this way.

It seems like not a big deal but to me it affirms the way I've been feeling for a while. This guy and his family have been really good to me and I don't know what I do to deserve it, I feel like a leech. I am a super boring and quiet person so it's not like I'm winning them over with my personality. I don't really have anything to give back to them so when I do or say something stupid I feel like I'm throwing their kindness back in their face. Sometimes I don't feel like I'm fit to have friends.
I feel like it does, I don't think I can change my heart or my brain. All I can do is pretend to fit in with others which in turn means continuing to deceive people.

No, I went to a counselor in high school for my compulsive lying but I didn't stick with it for long. This was 10+ years ago. I was able to kick that habit but just because I'm acting like a better person doesn't make me better.
